questions.stem: A service lift is descending but its downward speed is decreasing. Taking upward as positive, what direction must its net force point?

options.A: Upward, since its acceleration opposes its downward velocity.
options.B: Downward, because it is moving downward.
options.C: Zero, because the slowing is steady.
options.D: The direction cannot be inferred without its mass.

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Deceleration while descending is upward acceleration, not upward velocity.

rival_demands.rejection_rationale: Requires dynamic physical reasoning, not isolated recall.

factor_evidence.system_coupling: Score 1: Only the lift cabin's motion is evaluated.
factor_evidence.vector_dimensionality: Score 2: Up is chosen positive although velocity is downward.
factor_evidence.constraint_latency: Score 1: Mass and slowing trend are supplied directly.
factor_evidence.domain_coupling: Score 2: Translate change of velocity into acceleration then use Newton II.
factor_evidence.math_friction: Score 1: Only a sign inference, no equation system.

B.diagnostic: Incorrect: Velocity direction and acceleration direction need not agree.

C.diagnostic: Confuses the named system or the governing invariant; Deceleration while descending is upward acceleration, not upward velocity.

D.diagnostic: Fails the declared force/momentum direction or a dimensional check; At constant downward velocity a_y becomes zero.
